claims.text: Role in HSV: mucocutaneous: oral acyclovir, valacyclovir or famciclovir; herpes labialis alt: topical penciclovir or docosanol;
claims.quote: For mucocutaneous infections, consider oral acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir; for herpes labialis, an alternative is topical penciclovir or docosanol.

claims.text: recurrent or severe labialis: famciclovir 1500 mg as 1 dose or valacyclovir 2 g PO every 12 h for 1 day;
claims.quote: For recurrent or severe herpes labialis, famciclovir 1500 mg as 1 dose or valacyclovir 2 g orally every 12 hours for 1 day can be used.

claims.text: genital herpes (primary and recurrent): oral acyclovir, valacyclovir or famciclovir, most effective if started w.in 1 day of lesion onset;
claims.quote: Primary episodes and recurrences (reactivations) can be treated with oral acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir. Treatment is most effective when initiated within 1 day of lesion onset.

claims.text: early tx of a primary infection doesn't prevent recurrences;
claims.quote: However, even early treatment of primary infections does not prevent recurrences.

claims.text: pregnancy w genital herpes: acyclovir from 36 wks gestation ↓ recurrence and the need for C-section;
claims.quote: Pregnant patients who develop genital herpes lesions anytime during pregnancy can be given acyclovir starting at 36 weeks gestation to reduce the risk of a recurrence and thus the need for cesarean delivery

claims.text: immunocompromised, CNS infections or neonatal herpes: IV acyclovir;
claims.quote: For infections in immunocompromised patients, CNS infections, or neonatal herpes, IV acyclovir

claims.text: encephalitis: IV acyclovir for 14 to 21 days (prevents relapse).
claims.quote: Encephalitis is treated with IV acyclovir. Treatment for 14 to 21 days is preferred to prevent potential relapse
claims.locator: Treatment of Herpes Simplex Virus › CNS infections

claims.text: Safety: acyclovir AEs: phlebitis, renal dysfun, rarely neurotoxicity (lethargy, confusion, seizures, coma; USU w renal insuff);
claims.quote: Acyclovir is generally very well tolerated. However, adverse effects can include phlebitis, renal dysfunction, and, rarely, neurotoxicity (lethargy, confusion, seizures, coma; usually in the setting of renal insufficiency).
claims.locator: Treatment of Herpes Simplex Virus › CNS infections

claims.text: acyclovir-resistant strains are also resistant to penciclovir, famciclovir and valacyclovir; foscarnet may be effective.
claims.quote: Acyclovir-resistant strains are resistant to penciclovir, famciclovir, and valacyclovir. Foscarnet may be effective for acyclovir-resistant infections.

claims.text: Valacyclovir (Valtrex) label: cold sores: 2 g twice daily for 1 day, 12 h apart, at the earliest Sx;
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for treatment of cold sores is 2 grams twice daily for 1 day taken 12 hours apart. Therapy should be initiated at the earliest symptom of a cold sore (e.g., tingling, itching, or burning).

claims.text: initial genital herpes: 1 g twice daily for 10 days;
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for treatment of initial genital herpes is 1 gram twice daily for 10 days.

claims.text: recurrent: 500 mg twice daily for 3 days;
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for treatment of recurrent genital herpes is 500 mg twice daily for 3 days.

claims.text: suppression: 1 g once daily (500 mg once daily if ≤ 9 recurrences/yr).
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of VALTREX for chronic suppressive therapy of recurrent genital herpes is 1 gram once daily in patients with normal immune function. In patients with a history of 9 or fewer recurrences per year, an alternative dose is 500 mg once daily.

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to valacyclovir, acyclovir or any component.
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to valacyclovir (e.g., anaphylaxis), acyclovir, or any component of the formulation.

claims.text: TTP/HUS (some fatal) at 8 g/day in advanced HIV and transplant pts: stop at once if it occurs.
claims.quote: TTP/HUS, in some cases resulting in death, has occurred in patients with advanced HIV-1 disease and also in allogeneic bone marrow transplant and renal transplant recipients participating in clinical trials of VALTREX at doses of 8 grams per day. Treatment with VALTREX should be stopped immediately if clinical signs, symptoms, and laboratory abnormalities consistent with TTP/HUS occur.

claims.text: Acute renal failure: elderly, renal dz on doses too high for renal funct, nephrotoxic drugs or poor hydration; caution in elderly and ↓ dose in renal impairment.
claims.quote: Acute renal failure: May occur in elderly patients (with or without reduced renal function), patients with underlying renal disease who receive higher-than-recommended doses of VALTREX for their level of renal function, patients who receive concomitant nephrotoxic drugs, or inadequately hydrated patients. Use with caution in elderly patients and reduce dosage in patients with renal impairment.

claims.text: CNS AEs (agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures, encephalopathy), more likely in elderly: stop if they occur.
claims.quote: Elderly patients are more likely to have central nervous system adverse reactions. VALTREX should be discontinued if central nervous system adverse reactions occur
